jobs.description:
AI is changing not only what software we build, but how we build it. As our HiveAI Engineering Manager, you will lead the team at the centre of that shift. You will combine people leadership, strong engineering judgement and AI-assisted development to turn ideas into production-ready products faster.
This is an opportunity to help shape both a product and the way of working around it. You will build and lead a small, high-trust development team where AI accelerates engineering without compromising quality, security or maintainability.
About the role
As Engineering Manager for HiveAI, you lead the people and shape how the team works and delivers. You will lead an international team with developers based across several Fellowmind countries, so building trust, alignment and a strong team culture across locations will be an important part of your leadership.
You will work as a peer alongside our Product Manager and Chief Architect, each with a clear but closely connected area of ownership. The Product Manager drives the why and what. The Chief Architect sets the technical direction and guardrails. You lead the team and create the conditions for great engineering.
The way we build matters. The HiveAI team works from problems and hypotheses, using AI to move quickly from idea to experiment and prototype. What proves valuable is then hardened into secure, scalable and maintainable software. You will help define what this way of working looks like in practice as the team grows.
You will lead a team that brings together platform developers, who build and maintain HiveAI itself, and Frontier Fellows (Forward Deployed Engineers), who work close to our implementation teams and customers and bring what they learn and build back into the product. Your job is to bring these two perspectives together as one engineering team.
What you will do:
Build and lead the team. Own hiring, 1:1s, development and performance conversations, and build a strong, high-trust engineering culture across a distributed international team.
Design the way we deliver. Drive fast build-and-learn cycles, remove impediments and favour working demos and clear ship, change or stop decisions.
Turn prototypes into products. Together with the Chief Architect, make sure promising experiments cross the line into production with the engineering quality they need.
Make AI a real engineering capability. Coach developers in prompting, coding agents, AI-assisted testing and code review, and continuously evolve how the team works with AI.
Protect engineering understanding. AI should make engineers faster and help them learn, not become a substitute for understanding the systems they build.
Keep the focus on outcomes. Build a team that makes good decisions about what to build, how to build it and when AI is, and is not, the right tool.

Who are you?
You are a people leader who still thinks like an engineer.
You probably spent a significant part of your career as a software developer before moving into technical and people leadership. Today, you might be an Engineering Manager, Software Development Manager or a Tech Lead with people responsibility, ideally in a SaaS or software product company.
You are comfortable when the destination is clearer than the route to get there. You coach and enable your team, make good decisions with incomplete information and know when a fast prototype is good enough to learn from, but not good enough to ship.
We believe that you bring:
Extensive professional experience in software development, followed by at least 2–3 years of people leadership, either as an Engineering Manager or as a Tech Lead with direct people responsibility.
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agents, such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code or similar, as part of real software development.
Strong engineering practices across CI/CD, automated testing, code review and secure development.
Experience from a SaaS or software product environment, where teams own what they build beyond the first release.
Experience leading distributed or international teams, with the ability to coach, communicate and build a strong team culture across locations, mainly through digital ways of working.
Experience with Azure and the Microsoft technology stack, which is highly valuable given HiveAI's technology landscape.
The ability to start from a problem statement and a hypothesis, and to shape the route to a solution together with the team as you learn.
Professional proficiency in English and the local language of the country in which you are applying: Swedish, Danish or Dutch.

You do not need to be the person writing the most code in the team. What matters is your technical background. It gives you the credibility and judgement to coach great engineers and challenge decisions. It also lets you create an environment where they can move exceptionally fast without losing control of what they build.
What is HiveAI?
At Fellowmind, we're building HiveAI, a platform for developing, deploying and operating AI solutions at scale. It provides a secure and scalable foundation for enterprise AI and enables organisations to move beyond isolated experiments towards AI solutions that become part of how the business actually operates.
At its core is the HiveAI Technology, built on Microsoft Azure, which provides the foundation for deploying, scaling and managing AI agents securely. Around it sits the HiveAI Agent Lifecycle, helping organisations develop, deploy, manage and continuously improve their AI agents over time.
Why Fellowmind?
You will join HiveAI at a stage where there is still plenty to shape. You will have real influence on how the team, the product and the way of working take form, with an international organisation and the Microsoft ecosystem behind you.
Fellowmind combines deep industry knowledge and personal guidance with Microsoft cloud technology across ERP, cloud infrastructure, data & AI, CRM, intranet and Modern Workplace. We are an international organisation with more than 2,000 colleagues across Europe.
Our culture is built around putting people at the heart of what we do. We value collaboration, personal responsibility, development and the freedom to find a sustainable balance between work and life.

Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What this role is and what it isn’t
It is a senior are lead role with scope. You’ll run an organization that spans product, platform, and applied AI - with other managers, senior engineers, and AI agents reporting in - and you’ll be accountable for what that organization ships, how it operates, and the business outcomes it drives.
It is still close enough to the work that you can drop into a Tech Lead role on a hard problem when the situation demands it. We don’t measure leadership IC time as a percentage. We measure it as the ability to pick up the work and ship at the bar you’re asking of your team.
It isn’t a role for managers who think of themselves as engineering-adjacent. You need to be credible in code, design, and on-call - and you need to want to be.
It isn’t a role for leaders who only think about engineering. We expect you to reason end-to-end about the business - economics, product, GTM, customers - and to make calls that are best for the company, not just best for your team.

What we’re looking for
15+ years of engineering experience, including 6+ years of people management at a pre-IPO startup, scale-up or frontier tech company, and at least 2 years of managing managers. Strong IC track record before management.
You’ve run an engineering organization of 30+ with managers and senior engineers reporting in. You can speak concretely about how you structured the org, how you hired up to that scale, and what you’d do differently.
Still hands-on at the Tech Lead level: you can pick up an unfamiliar codebase, design and ship a non-trivial change, run an incident, and review code at a high bar. You haven’t let your engineering muscle atrophy.
You’ve thought hard about humans and AI agents on the same team. What humans should and shouldn’t delegate. How productivity gets measured when the unit of work is shifting. Strong opinions, lightly held.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving clarity at an organisational level, not just technically. You write the doc that aligns three teams instead of waiting for someone else to.
Deep technical credibility in at least one area - full-stack product (React/TypeScript + Go/Rust), platform and developer experience (Kubernetes, sandboxing, observability, CI/CD, application frameworks), or applied AI (training, evals, agent systems, model serving).
Cross-functional to your core and business-fluent: you work seamlessly across design, product, and go-to-market, and know how to bring people along with you; andable to reason end-to-end about unit economics, product strategy, GTM, and customer outcomes
Track record of building and growing teams: you’ve hired senior engineers others wanted to work with, grown managers under you who became great in their own right, and set up career growth and performance practices that didn’t require constant maintenance. People follow you between companies.
Based in Stockholm or London or ready to relocate — this is an on-site, 5-days-a-week role.

What you’ll do
In one sentence: Run the engineering organization that builds Lovable - humans and agents both - and stay close enough to the work to be the senior engineer in the room when it matters.
Lead engineering. Product, platform, and applied AI under one roof. Own the roadmap and the business outcomes the org is on the hook for.
Set technical direction across the org: drive the design docs and architectural decisions that span teams, push back hard on weak plans (including your own), and hold a high bar for what ships.
Shape engineering culture: how we ship, how we write code, how we hire, how we deploy agents. Set norms that outlast any single project.
Ship fast: at Lovable the question is always “how fast can we get this to users?” You bias toward production and pull research, prototypes, and experiments into reality on the order of days and weeks, not quarters.
Build the operating model for an engineering org where humans and AI agents work side by side. We’re inventing this in public, and you’ll set the patterns the rest of the company learns from.
Operate as a peer to the executive team. Own outcomes that span beyond engineering, make the company’s biggest calls alongside the rest of leadership, and translate them back into engineering work that matters.

Our tech stack
We’re building with tools that both humans and AI love:
Frontend: React, TypeScript
Backend: Go and Rust
Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, many LLM providers
Data: ClickHouse, Firestore, Spanner, BigQuery
DevOps & tooling: Kubernetes, gVisor-based sandboxing for agentic workloads, GitHub Actions, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Terraform
Local tooling: Nix, DevEnv

About your application
Please submit your application in English — it’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally — if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

 Ready to join us?
Help us unlock human creativity and build the future of software creation.

jobs.occupation: Cyber Security Unit Manager - Cyber, Risk & Assurance
jobs.employer_name: H & M Hennes & Mauritz GBC AB
jobs.description:
Job Description

As Unit Manager for Cyber Risk & Assurance, you will lead H&M Group’s capabilities for cyber risk management, governance, compliance and assurance, playing a key role in strengthening the organisation’s security, resilience and ability to manage cyber risk in line with its risk appetite and regulatory obligations. 
As a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team reporting to the CISO, you will share accountability for the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term development of the Cyber Security function. Working closely with leaders across business, technology and cyber security, you will help shape outcomes that balance business objectives, security needs and risk management across H&M Group. 
You will provide strategic leadership for H&M Group’s Cyber Risk & Assurance capability, bringing together Cyber Security Frameworks, Supply Chain Security Risk and Security Control Assurance. Through your leadership, you will drive the continued evolution of cyber risk management and control assurance. 
WHAT YOU WILL DO
Lead the strategic direction, maturity and long-term development of H&M Group’s Cyber, Risk & Assurance capability, defining and evolving the strategy, roadmap and operating model in alignment with business, technology and cyber security objectives. 
Contribute as a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team to the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term capability development. 
Drive the continued development and maturity of the Information Security Management System (ISMS), including frameworks, policies and governance structures that enable consistent and effective management of cyber risk across H&M Group. 
Provide oversight and assurance of cyber security risks and controls, promoting transparency, accountability and effective risk-based decision-making. 
Strengthen H&M Group’s approach to security policy and compliance, regulatory requirements, security control assurance and governance reporting. 
Drive the continued development of third-party and supply chain security risk management, ensuring risks are identified, assessed and managed through effective governance and oversight. 
Lead budgeting, resource and investment planning, vendor strategy and prioritisation to support Cyber Risk & Assurance and wider cyber security objectives. 
Foster a high-performing, collaborative and inclusive culture focused on strong accountability, continuous improvement and business value. 

Leadership as a Unit Manager  
As a Unit Manager and member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team, you provide strategic leadership for your unit while contributing to the overall direction and development of the Cyber Security function. You develop high-performing leadership teams, drive organisational effectiveness and capability development. You demonstrate enterprise leadership by collaborating across the business, influencing senior stakeholders and supporting decisions that create value beyond your own unit. 
WHO YOU ARE
We are looking for someone with: 
8+ years of people management experience in cyber security, technology risk, governance, compliance, assurance or a closely related field. 
Proven experience leading enterprise-scale cyber risk, governance, compliance or assurance capabilities in a complex global organisation. 
Proven experience leading through managers and developing high-performing leadership teams, with accountability for a multidisciplinary organisation and its outcomes. 
Experience as a member of a senior cyber security, technology, risk or enterprise leadership team, contributing to shared strategy, priorities, investment decisions and organisational outcomes beyond your own area of responsibility. 
Strong knowledge of cyber security risk management, governance, compliance and assurance principles, methodologies and operating models. 
Strong knowledge of security frameworks, policies, standards and controls, and experience translating regulatory and internal requirements into effective security governance. 
Strong understanding of third-party and supply chain security risk management in complex global environments. 
Experience establishing meaningful cyber risk, governance and assurance metrics and translating risk and control information into clear business implications, priorities and decisions. 
Experience managing significant budgets, investments, resources, sourcing arrangements and external partners, including strategic vendor relationships. 
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with proven experience engaging senior and executive stakeholders and communicating complex cyber risk, regulatory and assurance topics in a clear and pragmatic way. 
Sound judgement and decision-making capability in complex, uncertain and risk-sensitive situations. 

 

Additional Information

This is a fulltime permanent role based in Stockholm, Sweden. 
If you believe your experience, skills, and ambitions align with this role, please submit your CV in English.
Diversity, Inclusion, and Innovation 
At H&M Group, we're deeply committed to fostering a Diverse & Inclusive environment. We actively seek out qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, national origin, disability, or age. 
Our commitment to an inclusive workplace drives our dynamic and forward-thinking culture. Regardless of your background, origin, or preferences, your application is warmly welcomed. We value diverse perspectives and skills, and every applicant contributes to our vibrant, creative community. Join us and be part of the future we're building. 
Our Offer 
At H&M Group, you're not just joining a team – you're joining a value-driven culture and an expansive tech network. Enjoy perks like staff discount cards, flexible work arrangements, wellness benefits, parental support, and more. Here, you're encouraged to be yourself, experiment, and chart your own growth path. As you flourish, so do we, with opportunities to create tangible impacts and shape the future. 
WHO WE ARE​ 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.​ 
​We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. ​ 
​WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE ​ 
We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here. 
In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries. 
JOIN US​ 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.​ 
​Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.​ 
​ *We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.​

jobs.description: Job ID: 7501(Senior) Quantitative Analyst, Model Monitoring and Performance (permanent position)Are you a quantitative analyst with a knack for navigating complex databases and producing clear analysis? Do you have knowledge of credit risk processes and an interest in, or experience with, IRB, IFRS9 or similar models? Then this opportunity may be for you! Quantitative Analyst to join the Model Monitoring and Performance team (MMP) within Risk Models.Nordea are currently developing and implementing a suite of new, state-of-the-art IRB and IFRS9 models. MMP is responsible for ensuring that the new models’ performance is continuously scrutinized, and for identifying any issues arising within them. Further, we are responsible for assessing and overseeing how IRB models are used in credit processes, including whether model use is in line with regulations, internal requirements and the approved purpose of the models.Our key stakeholders are model developers, model users in Business and senior management. About our teamMeet the Model Monitoring and Performance team. Our role is to contribute to assessments of how IRB models are used in credit processes, communicate identified issues and help develop clear internal guidelines for appropriate model use.Our team is an inspiring, competent and creative group of professionals in an international environment. In your daily job, you’ll be applying your quantitative and data analysis skills to produce clear and concise communication about model performance and performance issues to model developers and senior management. You’ll mainly be working with Python, SQL and Snowflake, but SAS and other tools may be used here and there. The role will be located in Helsinki or Stockholm and team colleagues are in Stockholm, Helsinki and Copenhagen.Collaboration. Ownership. Passion. Courage. These are the values that guide us in how we work and how we make decisions – and that we imagine you share with us. What you’ll be doingMain responsibilities in this role:    Quantitative analysis of model performance for all components of IRB and/or IFRS9 models (PD, LGD, EAD).    Communicating conclusions of your analysis to model developers and senior management – in reports and meetings.    Developing, maintaining and operating the IRB and IFRS9 model performance monitoring frameworks.    Collaborating with a variety of stakeholders including risk management, model development, model validation and model users across the bank.    Assessing how IRB models are used in credit processes, identifying potential gaps against regulatory and internal requirements, and communicating conclusions and follow-up needs.Who you areThis is the right role for you if you:    Are driven by a desire to know more.    Love to make sense of data.    Are self-driven and take ownership.    Find it easy to understand others, and make yourself understood by others.    Love to think in terms of the big picture, but know that the devil is in the details.    Enjoy learning, and are excited about bringing your ideas to the table.    Are honest and reliable, and willing to speak up even when it’s difficult.    Think it is important to get governance right.Your background and skills include:    Master’s in a quantitative field such as mathematics, engineering, econometrics, data science, finance, or similar.    Excellent communication skills (English is the working language).    Sound knowledge of applied mathematical modelling and excellent quantitative skills.    Proficiency in Python and SQL.    Knowledge of credit risk processes and how risk models and parameters are used in credit assessment and decision-making.    Knowledge of or interest in IRB, IFRS9 or similar models – practical experience with model use, monitoring or governance is a definitive plus.What we offerPeople come here when they want to get somewhere. For some, it’s to take their career to the next level. Natural Cycles is a regulated medical device company that markets like a consumer brand, which is exactly what makes the creative work here harder and better. We are rebuilding the brand to match the science, launching our first wearables, and doing it with a creative team that is being rebuilt at the same time. You are the senior art direction craft in that team: the person who takes a brief and comes back with a point of view, sets the visual bar on the work you touch, and makes the brand hold together across a campaign film, a carousel and a packaging insert. This is a senior individual contributor seat. You set the standard through the work rather than through a reporting line.Please note: this role is open only to candidates who already live on the U.S. East Coast or in Stockholm, Sweden. We are not able to offer relocation support. What you will be doing    Art-direct campaign and brand work from concept to production-ready across film, digital, social, out-of-home, packaging and event.    Lead the visual execution of product launches, working from the brand platform rather than restating it each time.    Make brand and performance push in the same direction: develop work that holds the brand standard and earns its place in a test.    Build systems, not only assets — templates, components, type and grid behaviour, chart and graphic styles that stay coherent as volume grows and more hands touch them.    Direct external partners: photographers, directors, illustrators, retouchers, production and agency teams, and localisation partners adapting work for individual markets.    Work with Product Design and Writing so the brand does not change character at the app boundary.    Use AI tooling as part of daily production — motion, variation, concepting — and have a view on where it fails.    Work inside medical device and advertising constraints, and partner with Regulatory early enough that review is fast rather than adversarial.What skills and experience we think you have    8+ years in art direction or design, with a portfolio of integrated work — not a single channel — that performed as well as it looked.    Evidence of range: a brand idea carried across formats, from a hero moment down to a paid unit.    Systems thinking. Has built templates and components other people actually used.    Fluency in Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud; working motion ability, with After Effects or equivalent.    Proven quick turnarounds without a drop in craft.    Comfort working inside a regulated health brand, including Legal and Regulatory review rounds.    Health, wellness or femtech experience is an advantage, as is illustration or 3D for launch moments.    Currently based on the U.S. East Coast, or in Stockholm, Sweden.What we offer    Flexible work arrangement - you will be part of a team spread across the U.S. East Coast and Sweden that values effective collaboration and transparent communication, irrespective of work location    Professional development - you will work alongside knowledgeable colleagues in the continuous growth and skill enhancement environment    Modern technology - you will leverage innovative technologies and tools, within an environment that empowers you to contribute ideas and take ownership of your work    Impactful projects - you will contribute to groundbreaking projects that redefine industry standards and create tangible value    Commitment to quality - you will join a dynamic and progressive organization that prioritizes profitable, long-term product development LocationWe are a remote-friendly company, and we also value connecting in person. The team you will be working with are spread across Sweden and the U.S., and for this role we are looking for someone currently based either on the U.S. East Coast, or in Stockholm, Sweden.Salary bracket: $100,000 - $150,000 per year, annual bonus aligned with the Company’s Bonus Policy. Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate's skills, experience, and qualifications.This range may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will fall toward the starting point of the range, compensation will depend on the candidate's specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role's requirements.How to applyTo apply, just upload your CV and answer the questions on the application form. Company description:Who are we?Volvo Cars is a company on a mission; to bring traditional car manufacturing into a connected, sustainable and smart future.Since 1927, we have been a brand known for our commitment to safety, creating innovative cars that make life less complicated for our consumers. In 2010, we decided to transform our business, resulting in a totally new generation of cars and technologies, as well as steady growth and record sales. Today, we’re expanding our global footprint in Europe, China and the US, and we’re on the lookout for new talent. We are constantly pushing our own skills and abilities to drive change in the automobile industry like never before. We are looking for innovative, committed people to join us in this endeavour and create safe, sustainable and connected cars. We believe in the power of people and will challenge and support you to reach your full potential. Join us and be part of Volvo Cars’ journey into the future.Job description:   Join Lynk & Co Europe, powered by Volvo Cars’ commercial network   Lynk & Co is entering an exciting new phase in Europe. From January 2027, Volvo Cars will become its exclusive European distributor, creating a new commercial set-up that combines Volvo Cars’ established infrastructure with Lynk & Co’s bold and distinctive brand. Employed by Volvo Cars and working closely with Lynk & Co, you’ll have the opportunity to help build this new chapter from the ground up and contribute to the brand’s continued growth across Europe.     What you'll do   As a Warranty Specialist, you will be part of the Warranty team within Aftersales, supporting our European workshop and retailer network. You will play a key role in our daily warranty operations by assessing warranty claims, supporting workshops and retailers, and ensuring that warranty decisions are accurate, consistent and aligned with applicable warranty policies and technical requirements. The role combines technical and financial claim assessment with workshop support, warranty cost control, data analysis and the recovery of eligible warranty costs from manufacturing plants, suppliers and other responsible parties. You will also contribute to the continuous improvement of warranty processes, claim quality and workshop support across European operations. •    Review and assess warranty claims submitted by workshops and make decisions within delegated authority.•    Verify claim eligibility, technical diagnosis, repair information, labour operations, parts usage, costs and supporting documentation.•    Use Lynk & Co technical information and relevant systems, including Codiac, to support consistent and evidence-based warranty decisions.•    Assess whether repairs and parts replacements are technically justified and appropriately documented.•    Provide clear and constructive guidance to workshops and retailers on warranty requirements, claim corrections and required documentation.•    Identify recurring claim-quality issues, unusual cost patterns and potential product-quality concerns.•    Prepare and follow up cases for warranty cost recovery from manufacturing plants, suppliers and other responsible parties.•    Coordinate warranty-related parts returns and provide relevant warranty information to Quality and other stakeholders.•    Analyse claim trends, cost deviations and workshop patterns, and contribute to warranty reporting and KPI follow-up.•    Maintain accurate and traceable warranty documentation and contribute to audits where required.•    Contribute to continuous improvements in warranty processes, working methods and workshop guidance.   Success in the role is measured through the quality, consistency and efficiency of warranty claim handling, timely workshop support, accurate documentation, effective warranty cost control, successful recovery of eligible warranty costs and contribution to the continuous improvement of Warranty operations.     What you'll bring   •    Relevant experience in automotive warranty, aftersales, technical support, claims handling or a comparable field.•    Good understanding of automotive repair processes and workshop operations.•    Ability to accurately assess technical and financial information.•    Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.•    Ability to interpret warranty policies, procedures and technical documentation.•    Good digital skills and confidence working across multiple systems.•    Good written and verbal communication skills in English.•    Ability to manage multiple cases and priorities effectively.•    Ability to make objective, consistent and well-documented decisions.•    Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team. Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage:•    Automotive manufacturer, importer, national sales company or authorised workshop network.•    Automotive warranty or claim-management systems.•    Codiac or comparable automotive technical and support systems.•    Workshop support, warranty cost recovery or warranty data analysis.•    Microsoft Power BI or similar reporting and analytics tools.

Company description:Ericsson ABJob description:   Join our Team     About this opportunityEricsson is looking for an intellectual property lawyer to join the IPR Policy Research Team. The role helps policymakers and potential licensees understand Ericsson's leadership in 5G and 6G, including its role in standardisation and its strong cellular patent portfolio. It combines legal expertise, policy research and strategic communication, and suits someone who can explain complex IP and technical topics clearly and engagingly.   What you will do•    Research and draft policy papers, position papers and other publications on Standard Essential Patents (SEPs), FRAND terms and standardisation policy.•    Develop clear, engaging content, such as infographics and videos, for policymakers and industry stakeholders.•    Work with technical and legal colleagues to identify key messages on Ericsson's 5G and 6G innovation.•    Prepare summaries of relevant FRAND-related court decisions and support internal and external communication.•    Review collaboration agreements and coordinate collaborations with universities.•    Support video recordings, including logistics and script preparation.   What you bring•    A law degree with a specialisation in intellectual property and at least two years of experience in a law firm or equivalent IP environment.•    An understanding of SEPs and FRAND licensing principles.•    Excellent written and spoken English.•    The ability to translate complex legal and technical concepts into accessible, persuasive messages.•    An interest in communication and marketing, with an eye for clarity and audience engagement.•    A structured, proactive and collaborative approach.•    A Master's or PhD in IP or a related field, and experience writing policy or industry papers, are an advantage.

Company description:At NKT in Karlskrona, we develop and manufacture high voltage power cables that enable the transition to renewable energy. Here, you will be part of an international engineering centre with advanced high voltage test halls, modern cable production and the cable laying vessel NKT Victoria. As Connectors, we collaborate to develop innovative technology that connects a greener and more sustainable world. NKT is headquartered in Denmark and operates in more than 30 countries.NKT - We connect a greener world. www.NKT.com.Job description:Shape competitive high-voltage cable solutions for the energy transitionDo you want to take technical ownership of complex tenders and help shape high-voltage cable systems that enable the transition to renewable energy? As a Tender Lead Engineer at NKT, you will translate customer requirements and tender strategy into compliant and executable HVAC and HVDC cable system solutions. You will combine advanced engineering with technical leadership and customer interaction, working across disciplines and functions in an international environment. This is an opportunity to support key technical decisions at an early stage, contribute directly to NKT’s business growth and work with critical power infrastructure supporting the expansion and interconnection of power grids. Manage engineering from tender strategy to technical solutionAs Tender Lead Engineer, you will take end-to-end technical ownership of assigned tenders, from requirement analysis and solution development through technical submission, clarification and handover. Acting as the technical focal point, you will coordinate multidisciplinary engineering activities and ensure the proposed cable system balances technical performance, manufacturability, installation constraints, qualification, risk, cost and schedule. Key responsibilities include:•    Coordinate the complete technical scope and engineering activities of assigned tenders•    Develop and optimize HVAC and HVDC cable system solutions•    Translate requirements and standards into design premises and engineering deliverables•    Manage technical risks, deviations, qualifications and opportunities•    Lead technical customer dialogues, clarifications and negotiations The position is primarily based in Karlskrona but Malmö, Västerås or Rotterdam may also be considered. Regular collaboration across NKT locations is expected, with travel for customer meetings, internal collaboration and tender activities when required. A technical leader with a commercial mindsetYou thrive in a complex technical environment where ownership, structure and collaboration are key. You communicate clearly, build trust and stay focused when priorities shift. You are comfortable working across teams and locations, and you enjoy bringing people together to reach clear decisions. In addition, we believe you bring:•    M.Sc. or Ph.D. in electrical engineering or another relevant engineering discipline, or equivalent technical experience•    Relevant experience in tender engineering, project engineering, cable system design, power transmission or a comparable technically complex industry•    Demonstrated ability to manage and coordinate multidisciplinary technical work with responsibility for scope, quality and deadlines•    Demonstrated capability in requirement analysis, technical documentation and structured risk-based decision-making•    Fluency in spoken and written English•    Experience with high-voltage cable systems, relevant standards, qualification or installation interfaces is an advantage Lead engineering for tomorrow’s energy infrastructureNKT is committed to fostering a diverse organization and a culture where people from different backgrounds can thrive and are inspired to perform at their best. We believe that a diverse organization enables sustainable performance, and that an inclusive and welcoming culture makes for a better place to work. At NKT, you will work at the intersection of engineering, customer needs and commercial strategy, gaining broad exposure to high-voltage cable systems and international tender projects. You will collaborate with specialists across engineering and other functions while developing both your technical leadership and commercial understanding. Your work will contribute directly to cable solutions that support renewable energy integration, power grid expansion and the electrification of society. Read more about our offer and listen to some voices of NKT Connectors here! We will review applications continuously, but we recommend you apply no later than 2026-12-21. An extract from the criminal record, alcohol- and drug tests, medical tests along with personality tests, will be part of our recruitment process. jobs.description: Job DescriptionWHAT YOU WILL DOShape how we connect with our customers across the world, through marketing touchpoints. As a Channel and Content Planner, you will develop detailed and strategic content plans for one or more marketing channels. You will ensure the communication across your channel reflects campaign priorities and seasonal activations, working closely with marketing planning and creative teams. You will own content briefs and collaborate with stakeholders across Media, Creative, Product, and Local Marketing Teams to deliver on timelines and objectives.      Own what meets the customer in your channel(s).     Connect business priorities to an execution plan for content activated in your channel(s).     Maintain a holistic brand and business mindset, balancing short and long-term growth potential.     Build detailed, channel-specific briefs that support the execution of the marketing plan globally and in key markets.     Maintain a solid understanding of your channel, competitors, and customer context.     Ensure channel plans reflect channel behaviour and audience.     Connect insights to an activation plan and content framework that secures channel growth. WHO YOU ARE In this role, we’re looking for someone who combines strategic thinking with a collaborative mindset. You’ll thrive if you’re curious, proactive, and confident in your ideas, while staying open to input and feedback.  We are looking for people with…     3+ years of experience in marketing, communication, content planning, or channel management.     Structured, with the ability to prioritise, challenge, and align tasks across multiple time horizons.     Experience in developing detailed content plans and writing briefs for specific channels, while aligning with organisational goals and KPI targets. Experience in launching new or emerging marketing channels for a multi-national company is a bonus.      And people who have…     Positive service-minded mindset and great administration skills.     Demonstrated collaboration skills to work effectively with cross-functional stakeholders.      Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.      WHO WE ARE H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make. We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future.  WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits and extensive development opportunities across the globe. You’ll be part of a collaborative environment where your ideas matter.
